approach: Add one new module, crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs, holding `check_reading_coverage(reading, request)`. It finds the request's `Acceptance:` bullets and reduces each bullet and each criterion to a set of content stems. A bullet's score is the share of its own stems found in its best-matching single criterion, with no stripping of words the request prose repeats and no uniqueness rule. A bullet below a tuned integer-percent threshold (40) is omitted. Any omitted bullet refuses the reading, naming the bullet, unless the request's non-bullet text affirmatively allows a split. Readings that ask a question or decline, and requests with no `Acceptance:` heading, are not checked. Wiring: `mod coverage; pub use coverage::*;` in reading.rs and one `step!(check_reading_coverage(reading, request));` line in `refusing_check`, placed after `check_scope_limit` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`, so `check_reading_references` stays the last step. Existing refusals still come first. Tests are unit tests in coverage.rs plus new refusal_corpus cases. A tuning test prints the per-bullet scores and a replay test prints the refusal rate over the recorded shapes. CHANGELOG and the doc comment state the change. fake.rs and drain.rs are touched only if the suite fails without them.

decisions.choice: Score each bullet by matched_stems*100 >= total_stems*COVERAGE_MIN_PERCENT (40) against its single best criterion. Stems come from lowercase alphanumeric runs. Function words are dropped from a fixed stop list, and tokens under 2 characters are dropped. A suffix is stripped in the order ing, ed, es, s, applied only when 3 or more characters remain and the word does not end in `ss`. Then a trailing `e` is dropped, and a doubled final consonant left by stripping ed or ing (not l, s or z) is collapsed. So flagged/flag, queued/queue, names/named and ordering/order meet.
decisions.reason: Fixes the earlier rejection: no word is discarded for being repeated in the prose. The bp5e bullet 'The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates' has 7 content stems (root, cause, nam, chang, description, fix, originat). The criterion 'its doc comment names the root cause' shares 3 of them, 43%. The ttnw pair shares 4 of 6 stems, 67%. 40% accepts both with a margin, and a tuning test asserts the lowest covered score is at least the threshold and the highest omitted score is below it. Integer math avoids float comparisons.

rejected.option: Strip words the request prose repeats and require stem uniqueness
rejected.why: The rejected design of 20261029-111121-fzx0: a bullet whose only distinguishing words are repeated in the prose became empty and vacuously covered.

rejected.option: Substring or exact-text match of the bullet inside a criterion
rejected.why: Readers paraphrase (bp5e, ttnw), so it would refuse nearly every real reading.

rejected.option: A model call to judge coverage
rejected.why: Reading checks are deterministic and call no model (checks.rs doc comments); it would add cost and flakiness.

decisions.choice: Check only bullets under an `Acceptance:` or `Acceptance criteria:` heading line (trimmed, case-insensitive, leading # or * ignored). A bullet is a line that passes `is_bullet`. The section ends at the first non-empty non-bullet line.
decisions.reason: The brief says requests with no Acceptance heading are not checked. Many existing requests and tests carry bare bullets with no heading (job_plan.rs:166, drain.rs:3988, 4067, 4492, 4678, 6317, and the corpus cases 'star-bullets' and 'numbered-dot-parts'). Checking them would refuse readings the owner never constrained, and would break the fake-reader tests. The `1)` and `(a)` forms are not read by `is_bullet` today, and the existing corpus pins that as a known gap.

rejected.option: Treat every bullet as acceptance, as `request_text_acceptance` does for `athena plan`
rejected.why: Widens the refusal rate far beyond the 10% estimate and refuses plain lists.

decisions.choice: A request allows a split when a sentence of its non-bullet text, lowercased, has a whole-phrase match (using the existing `has_phrase`) on one of: 'may split', 'can split', 'could split', 'free to split', 'allowed to split', 'ok to split', 'okay to split', 'split is allowed', 'split is fine', 'split is ok', 'split it', 'split this job', 'split the job', 'split into'. It must also have no negation word (not, never, no, don't, dont, without, avoid, forbid, must) in the same sentence. 'Do not split this job' therefore allows nothing.
decisions.reason: The brief requires affirmative wording only and names 'Do not split' as the negative example. A phrase list with a negation guard is deterministic and testable. It is a text floor, as `replay_declaration` is.

rejected.option: Any occurrence of the word 'split' allows a split
rejected.why: 'Do not split this job' would disable the check, which is the failure sza7 shows.

decisions.choice: Insert the step after `check_scope_limit` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.
decisions.reason: Every existing refusal still comes first, so corpus expectations for earlier checks are unchanged. `check_reading_references` stays the last step, as docs/decisions.md line 3923 states. The check_* order tests in reading.rs (about lines 4897, 5379, 7402, 8101) assert only the relative position of other steps, which this does not change.

rejected.why: Contradicts the 'runs last' statement in D-record 3923 and the doc of check_boundary_and_repo_files.

decisions.choice: The refusal names each omitted bullet (first 120 characters, with its marker removed), its best share and the threshold. It tells the reader to cover the bullet in a criterion in the bullet's own words, or to ask the split as a question. A reading with `question` set is not checked, so the question path is open.
decisions.reason: Matches the contract that a split may be proposed only as a question, never by dropping a bullet, and the 'one correction' flow at reading.rs:722-731.

rejected.why: Listing a bullet as out of scope is exactly the split sza7 was rejected for.

decisions.choice: Keep 'expected 10% of newly refused readings' in the criteria and the CHANGELOG, labelled an estimate. State beside it the figure the fixture replay prints, for example 'fixture replay: R of N bullets-bearing readings refused, all omissions, 0 readings that cover every bullet'.
decisions.reason: records/ is not in the snapshot, so no replay over real history is possible. A fixture rate is not a sample of history, so presenting it as the expected share would mislead. `replay_declaration` reads 'N% of newly refused readings' (replay.rs `declared_percent`), so the phrase must keep that exact form; the hold limit is then 15% (`replay_limit_percent`).

rejected.why: The fixture set contains the deliberately rejected sza7 shape, so its rate is not the rate on history.

risks.risk: The 40% threshold sits close to the bp5e shape (about 43% with the corpus tail, 60% on the truncated bullet), so a small stemming change could flip it and wrongly refuse a reading that covers every bullet.
risks.mitigation: The tuning test prints each bullet's score and asserts min covered >= 40 > max omitted. The rebuilt sza7 shapes keep the omitted bullet at 20% or less. Moving a stem rule moves a printed number, which the test makes visible.

risks.risk: A real reading may paraphrase a bullet with few shared words (a 3-word bullet needs 2 of 3 stems) and be refused, raising the refusal rate above the 10% estimate.
risks.mitigation: The refusal names the bullet and its score, so the reader's one correction is to restate the bullet's words in a criterion. The declared share is 10%, so the hold limit is 15% and a bigger rise is held by the existing replay. Bullets with no content word after the stop list are treated as covered.

risks.risk: A cli test sends a request with an `Acceptance:` heading to the fake reader, and the reading is refused.
risks.mitigation: This is known now: the fallback in step 10 makes the fake reader emit a criterion per bullet. It is applied only when `cargo test --locked` shows a failure, and criterion 10 shows the diff is limited to that.

risks.risk: The corpus `INPUT_FORMS` array is a fixed-size `[&str; 52]`. A forgotten length bump or an unused tag fails `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms`.
risks.mitigation: Step 7 sets the length to 59 and each new tag is carried by at least one new case, listed in the plan. The test is run in the demonstration for criterion 5.

risks.risk: A split phrase list will miss some affirmative wordings (a false refusal) and may let through an odd negated one.
risks.mitigation: A refused reading can always ask the split as a question, which is not checked. The phrase table test pins the accepted and refused forms.
